text:
ConocoPhillips rose 0.74% today, recovering from a sharp 2.2% drop on October 27th that followed oil price weakness. The modest gain reflects conflicting signals in crude markets: while U.S. oil prices are holding firm at $103/barrel, geopolitical uncertainty around Iran has created a seesaw effect. Yesterday's news of renewed U.S.-Iran peace talks eased supply-disruption fears and weighed on oil prices Thursday, but today's reports of military leadership changes and continued Trump administration ambiguity on Iran policy have kept investors cautious rather than decisively bullish.

Over two weeks, the stock is up 4.72%, tracking the broader oil price strength — U.S. crude has roughly kept pace, and global oil at $123/barrel remains elevated. The energy sector has been volatile on Middle East tensions, but with the geopolitical backdrop still unresolved and policy signals mixed, the stock is consolidating rather than trending sharply either direction.
